skill.name: wiki-onboarding
skill.description: Generates architecture and contributor onboarding guides for a codebase, using repository evidence and line citations.
skill.summary: Create evidence-based architecture and contributor onboarding guides.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: New contributors need clear context before they can work safely. This skill turns repository evidence into architecture and contributor guides.
actual_capabilities: Creates a principal-level architecture guide focused on design decisions and system tradeoffs.
Creates a practical contributor guide with setup, workflow, testing, and debugging sections.
Detects the main project language from common build and manifest files.
Requires file and line citations for claims about the codebase.
Includes Mermaid diagrams for architecture, data flow, dependency, and workflow views.
Covers security model, operational concerns, technical debt, and common pitfalls.
limitations: Accuracy depends on accessible repository files and current code comments.
It does not execute tests or verify setup commands by itself.
Generated guidance may need review for private links, contacts, or policies.
It cannot infer undocumented business context with full certainty.

use_cases.title: Onboard New Engineers
use_cases.description: Create a practical path through setup, project structure, tests, debugging, and first contribution steps.

use_cases.title: Explain System Architecture
use_cases.description: Build a senior-level guide that explains design principles, dependencies, tradeoffs, failure modes, and operational concerns.

use_cases.title: Prepare Repository Documentation
use_cases.description: Generate evidence-backed wiki pages with diagrams and citations before a handoff, audit, or open source release.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Onboarding Guide
prompt_templates.scenario: You need starter documentation for a repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create onboarding documentation for this repository. Include the architecture guide and contributor guide described by the wiki-onboarding skill.

prompt_templates.title: New Contributor Walkthrough
prompt_templates.scenario: A new teammate needs a practical first week guide.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate the Zero-to-Hero contributor guide for this codebase. Focus on setup, first task, tests, debugging, and common pitfalls.

prompt_templates.title: Principal Architecture Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Senior engineers need system context before planning changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate the Principal-Level onboarding guide. Emphasize design principles, key abstractions, data flow, failure modes, security model, and technical debt.

prompt_templates.title: Evidence-Backed Wiki Package
prompt_templates.scenario: You need publishable wiki pages for a complex repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create both onboarding guides with file and line citations for every claim. Add Mermaid diagrams for architecture, data flow, dependencies, and workflows.

output_examples.input: Create onboarding documentation for a TypeScript service repository.
output: A principal guide explaining architecture, data flow, dependencies, failure modes, and operational concerns.
A contributor guide covering setup, project structure, first task, tests, debugging, and quick reference notes.
Mermaid diagrams and line citations that connect guidance to repository evidence.

output_examples.input: Help a staff engineer understand why this repository is structured this way.
output_examples.output: The result is an architecture-focused guide with design principles, major decisions, dependency rationale, security model, and known technical debt.

output_examples.input: Prepare docs for new open source contributors.
output_examples.output: The result is a contributor walkthrough with prerequisites, setup steps, development workflow, testing guidance, common pitfalls, glossary, and quick reference.

best_practices: Run it on a clean repository state so citations match current files.
Review generated setup commands before sharing them with new contributors.
Remove private contacts, internal links, and sensitive operational details before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a substitute for security review or threat modeling.
Do not publish generated architecture details without checking confidentiality requirements.
Do not accept uncited claims when repository evidence should exist.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It generates two onboarding guides: an architecture deep dive and a practical contributor walkthrough.

faq.question: Does it support multiple programming languages?
faq.answer: Yes. It looks for common build files to choose language-specific examples for major ecosystems.

faq.question: Does it require citations?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill instructs the assistant to ground claims in file and line citations.

faq.question: Can it create diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It requests Mermaid diagrams for architecture, data flow, dependencies, and workflows.

faq.question: Will it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes documentation structure and command examples, but it does not include executable scripts.

faq.question: Should teams review the output?
faq.answer: Yes. Teams should verify accuracy and remove private operational details before publication.
